should_fix.issue: Readers who are buying want a pointer on money (does shape change cost per carat?), and the intro's 'no prices' leaves that question with nowhere to go.
should_fix.fix: Keep the no-prices stance. Right after 'No grading tables, no prices, no rules.' add one sentence sending the money side to the diamond guide, e.g. 'For the money side, our [diamond buying guide](/style-advice/diamond-buying-guide) covers how the 4Cs shape value.' Do not state any price, per-carat figure or cost ranking by shape. (The link-map row for that guide is still 'draft'; it must be live before this post publishes.)

consider.issue: The intro says 'eight shapes' but never names them, so the answer to the search isn't in the first 100 words.
consider.fix: Apply. Name all eight in the intro sentence: 'This guide covers eight shapes: round brilliant, oval, emerald, cushion, princess, pear, marquise and radiant.' Leave the 4 takeaways as they are (exactly 4, one sentence each).

consider.issue: The comparison table, the part readers want to screenshot, sits after all eight long sections.
consider.fix: Apply. Move the whole '## Engagement ring cuts compared' section (heading, intro line and table) to straight after '## Key takeaways' and before '## Cut or shape?'. Keep the H2 wording, which carries the keyword.

consider.issue: 'Table', 'crown' and 'pavilion' are used without explanation (first uses: 'large table' in the emerald practical note, 'high crown' under Asscher, 'deep pavilion' under princess).
consider.fix: Apply. On first use only, add a short plain gloss: table (the large flat facet on top), crown (the upper part of the stone, above its widest edge), pavilion (the lower part, below that edge). These are standard anatomy terms, not claims. If the writer wants a citation, use GIA's diamond anatomy wording; if it can't be matched, add [[VERIFY: GIA wording for table, crown, pavilion]] rather than inventing a definition.

consider.issue: 'Historic, revived' in the marquise table row isn't backed by the body, which mentions Louis XV but no revival.
consider.fix: Apply. The revival is sourced in fact_31, so make the body carry it: extend the Louis XV line with 'It was popular again in the Edwardian era and from the 1970s to the 1990s, and is attracting renewed interest. <!-- fact_31 -->' The table cell 'Historic, revived' then stands. If the writer prefers not to touch the body, change the cell to 'Historic, dramatic' (fact_26 calls the marquise shape dramatic) instead. Do one or the other, not both.

consider.issue: 'GIA says' opens almost every 'Suits' line (10 uses), so it reads like a summary of GIA's site with no house voice.
consider.fix: Apply. Vary the attribution (e.g. 'According to GIA', 'GIA's view is', or a fact sentence with the source in the comment marker) and add a short brand-voice line in 3 or 4 shape sections that interprets the sourced fact for a couple, such as how it sits with a wedding band or reads in a close-up photo. Every new sentence must restate a sourced fact or be clearly opinion/preference; no new claims about wedding experience, numbers of weddings or 'we've seen'.

consider.issue: The outdoor-light angle is the one part that feels like wedding people rather than a jeweller, and the primary reader wants more of it.
consider.fix: Apply, from sourced facts only. Shapes without an 'In outdoor light' line can get one built from: round brilliant, most brightness of all cuts (fact_14); cushion, softer sparkle in the brilliant style or a 'crushed ice' look in the modified style (fact_21); radiant, brilliant-style faceting and a 'crushed ice' look (fact_32); princess, brilliant cut (fact_03), so sparkle rather than broad flashes (fact_02). Keep emerald, oval, pear and marquise lines as they are. No claims about how a shape photographs in sun or at a set time of day beyond these facts.

consider.issue: No date on the page, so readers can't tell if it's current.
consider.fix: Apply. Add 'last_updated: 2026-10-28' to the front matter (and update it at the final stage if the date changes).

consider.issue: The concierge paragraph is an unproven service claim: fee model, commission, how payments and deposits work, AUD quotes, a phone or named Advisor, real weddings, guest-travel detail, scale (200 to 400 guests, exclusive use, security, NDAs), a private channel.
consider.fix: Deferred business items: no copy change in this post. The editor already replaced the line with the brand-facts wording and 'the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins', and removed 'anywhere in the world' and 'first idea'. Log the reader questions for Nic and the /wonderland-concierge page; do not add proof, numbers or examples here unless Nic supplies them.

keep: The intro line 'No grading tables, no prices, no rules. Just proportion, preference and light.' Praised by planner_couple, funding_parent and uhnw; it is the trust signal for the whole piece.
The plain shape-versus-cut explanation in 'Cut or shape?', including 'GIA grades cut only on round brilliants' (funding_parent, sceptic, search_visitor).
The honest 'GIA gives no hand or finger guidance for the cushion, so the honest answer is to try it on.' (planner_couple, sceptic)
The three-step try-on routine, especially 'Photograph from above, then at arm's length' and 'That includes the daylight of an outdoor ceremony.' (planner_couple)
Practical setting notes on princess, pear and marquise points (funding_parent).
The FAQ answers that name GIA, including 'This is about appearance, not value.' (sceptic)
Named, checkable sourcing throughout; vary how GIA is attributed but do not remove the attributions or fact markers.
The 4 key takeaways, one sentence each.
conflicts_resolved: Concierge paragraph: four personas raised it, which would normally make it must-fix, but every remaining ask is a deferred business item (fee model, commission, deposits, named Advisor or phone, real weddings, private channel, scale) and the money-accountability gap is already closed by the editor's 'fee is agreed in writing' line. No facts exist to add, so it is logged, not fixed in copy.

Prices: sceptic and search_visitor want price direction; funding_parent, planner_couple and uhnw praised the no-price stance. The brief's primary reader (planner_couple) wants a calm style guide without a sales pitch, so the stance stays and a single pointer to the diamond guide answers the question without stating prices.

Brand voice versus sourcing: planner_couple wants more house view, sceptic values the strict GIA sourcing. Resolved for the primary persona with interpretation lines that rest on sourced facts, never new claims.
uhnw wants scale and discretion signals; the brief targets a dreaming-stage couple in their mid 30s, not UHNW planning. Not acted on in this post.

Gate: weighted enquiry likelihood is 1.6 against a 3.8 threshold, so the gate is 'revise'. That gap is structural, not a copy fault: this is a dreaming-stage ring article whose goal is a click to /destinations, and every reader said they would not enquire from a ring guide. The listed fixes will raise clarity and relevance; they will not move enquiry likelihood to 3.8, and the writer should not add sales pressure to try. Recommend the orchestrator treat this revise as a one-round polish (no re-panel loop).

Must-fix only where 3+ personas, primary-persona high, or money/legal/accountability trust loss; deferred business items excluded

Outdoor-light fixes tied to named source facts only
Takeaways kept at exactly 4 one-sentence bullets
